# E-E-A-T

*Concept* · also written EEAT

Experience, expertise, authoritativeness and trustworthiness: the qualities Google's rater guidelines ask raters to judge content by.

**Glossary** (*E-E-A-T*): Experience, expertise, authoritativeness and trust, from Google's rater guidelines: first-hand experience, the necessary knowledge or skill, and being a go-to source. Trust comes first: untrustworthy pages have low E-E-A-T however expert they seem.

5 claims mention it: 5 shown or said at the event (3 confirmed by Google docs, 1 consistent with Google docs, 1 nothing to verify). A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [Creating helpful, reliable, people-first content](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content), [General Guidelines](https://static.googleusercontent.com/media/guidelines.raterhub.com/en//searchqualityevaluatorguidelines.pdf).

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D3-C162`](../sessions/D3-S05-how-google-thinks-about-quality.md) Slide, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: The rater guidelines' table of contents shown on Google's slide covers page quality rating, YMYL topics, main and supplementary content, website and creator reputation, E-E-A-T and lowest quality pages. `[D3-C162, slide, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C222`](../sessions/D3-S06-uncovering-trustworthy-experiences-on-discover.md) Slide, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: Google's Discover slide defined E-E-A-T: experience means first-hand, personal experience with the topic, expertise the necessary knowledge or skill, and authoritativeness the extent to which the creator or website is known as a go-to source for the topic. `[D3-C222, slide, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C223`](../sessions/D3-S06-uncovering-trustworthy-experiences-on-discover.md) Slide, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: Google's Discover slide said trust comes first: untrustworthy pages have low E-E-A-T however experienced, expert or authoritative they seem. `[D3-C223, slide, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C218`](../sessions/D3-S06-uncovering-trustworthy-experiences-on-discover.md) Slide, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Google's Discover slide showed an eligibility gate: content with a policy violation goes to a policy compliance check and low-quality content to an E-E-A-T quality check, and both can end with the content filtered out, while safe and trusted content becomes eligible for Discover. `[D3-C218, slide, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D1-C292`](../sessions/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) Stage, Day 1, nothing to verify: A community speaker suggested that LLMs pick up some of Google's years of work on judging honesty and trust (E-E-A-T) by proxy, because they send many queries (probably fan-out queries) to search engines. `[D1-C292, stage, Thiago Pojda, Day 1]`
